what: Bindings to the Rust regex Crate Through the rure C API
title: Bindings to the Rust regex Crate Through the rure C API
text: (R-) rure provides high-performance regex operations using Rust regex crate (rure C API). NOTE: package development subject significant change. rure docs: rure C API Rust’s regex library, guarantees linear time searching using finite automata. exchange, must give common regex features backreferences arbitrary lookaround. however include capturing groups, lazy matching, Unicode support word boundary assertions. matching semantics generally correspond Perl’s, “leftmost first.” Namely, match locations reported correspond first match found backtracking engine. Regular expressions must UTF-8 compliant determined using Rust’s str::from_utf8(). However, haystacks UTF-8 compliant conversion UTF-8 performed. Whether invalid UTF-8 matched depends regular expression - see ‘Text encoding’ section rure C API. Care must taken ensure expected behaviour.

title: Detect regex matches — re_detect
text: re_detect() re_set_detect(), logical vector length string. re_set_detect_each(), logical matrix one row per element string one column per pattern patterns.

title: Detect regex matches — re_detect
text: re_detect() returns logical vector TRUE element string matches pattern FALSE otherwise. re_set_detect() set patterns, returning TRUE patterns match. re_set_detect_each() returns logical matrix one row per element string one column per pattern patterns - showing patterns match string. NA values string result NA output. Patterns must valid UTF-8 work Rust's regex engine. non-UTF-8 patterns result error.

title: Detect regex matches — re_detect
code: fruit <- c("apple", "banana", "pear", "pineapple") re_detect(fruit, "a") #> [1] TRUE TRUE TRUE TRUE re_detect(fruit, "^a") #> [1]  TRUE FALSE FALSE FALSE re_detect(fruit, "a$") #> [1] FALSE  TRUE FALSE FALSE re_detect(fruit, "b") #> [1] FALSE  TRUE FALSE FALSE re_detect(fruit, "[aeiou]") #> [1] TRUE TRUE TRUE TRUE  re_set_detect(fruit, c("a", "e")) #> [1] TRUE TRUE TRUE TRUE re_set_detect_each(fruit, c("a", "e")) #>      [,1]  [,2] #> [1,] TRUE  TRUE #> [2,] TRUE FALSE #> [3,] TRUE  TRUE #> [4,] TRUE  TRUE
